0.content:
Tugarin is Alyosha's black-and-white husky. He has blue eyes and wears a red scarf. Alyosha found him as an abandoned, starving pup and gave him his last two sausages, then walked off, because he could not afford a pet and was hunting a man-eating bear. The pup tracked him to his snow-cave ambush and barked at the bear, spoiling the clean shot. Alyosha fired on instinct and wounded the bear. Tugarin chased it down, and Alyosha found him standing proudly on the carcass. He gave in, said a hunter can't do without a hound, and named the pup Tugarin, hoping he would grow into a real bear-hound.

Tugarin answers hand signals and whistles. He distracts guards, follows scents such as Kresnik Kristall, and knows "Down" (prepare to attack) from "Sit" (stay). He dislikes being petted but loves treats. He once recognised Vodyanitsa's scent through a Rokot disguise. When Alyosha went to hunt his former comrades, he left Tugarin with his parents. In combat he appears through Alyosha's Elemental Burst.

Tugarin can count to ten and is helping train the puppies Whistle and Plate. He chases Vesna "like a butterfly". Alyosha breeds other dogs too and offers puppies to friends he trusts. His happiest memory in his Seal of Life was Tugarin's first catch, a rabbit hiding in the snow.

1.content:
Alatyr was a remote Snezhnayan village where aid took days to arrive. In an especially harsh winter, bandits robbed it of the villagers' last Mora and Kristall, and even their sawdust-stretched bread, and tried to burn the houses. Alyosha's parents fought them off with desperate resolve and were badly injured. That night the boy dug out the rifle his father had hidden under the floorboards for his coming of age. He cut ahead of the bandits through the wilds and killed every one of them before dawn. Afterwards he stood frozen among the bodies until noon. The bandits turned out to be penniless.

Desperate villagers later formed a group of "hunters" to raid the wilds, and Alyosha joined on one condition: they would rob only armed highwaymen, never ordinary travellers, and take no lives. That was the beginning of Alatyr's highwaymen. Nobody has lived in Alatyr for years, and the village is now remembered mostly for the gang that came from it.

2.comment: Alyosha: The war on the snowfields
2.content:
When Project Stuzha drove refugees across the tundra toward Nod-Krai, the Alatyr "hunters" broke their oath and preyed on them. Even the timid Taras was tempted. Alyosha felt responsible for giving them their teeth. He left Tugarin with his parents and waged a one-man war, firing on anyone who came near. The terror stopped travellers entering the deep snows at all, which kept them safe. The surviving highwaymen were left with one rule: never touch the "fowl". The Fatui arrived long after and closed the case as a bandit turf war.

Years later, after his mercy had made highwaymen bold, Alyosha walked into a staged robbery that was really an ambush. Taras, by then settled in town, broke the trap with wild, eyes-shut gunfire and told him the people still needed him. That moment gave Alyosha his ideal back: destroy evil that is beyond saving, and protect those who have not yet fallen.

3.content:
The Rokot is a covert Snezhnayan organisation that opposes Project Stuzha and tries to help ordinary people. Members take false identities, usually do not know one another, and choose their own methods as long as they do not use their anonymity to do evil. As Alyosha explained it to the Traveler, it gives the disaffected an outlet and exists in a grey area the Veche could crack down on at any time. Alyosha wrote to the Rokot's president about the Traveler, approval came quickly, and he handed them the application form at the Korolevskiy Theater.

A proud, mysterious man with bodyguards recruited Alyosha by testing his judgement about the "beasts" in his territory. Alyosha said he would join but would not take orders. The man answered that freedom was the Rokot's creed. The Rokot's files on Project Stuzha convinced him that the nation's real illness lay deeper than its criminals. Polonsky, a Fatui officer, has openly guessed that Alyosha is Rokot; Alyosha denied it.

4.content:
When the Traveler reached Sretomorozsk in 7.0, every inn was closed, households could not afford heat, and residents were fighting with the Fatui over Kristall quotas. Alyosha suspected the friendly liaison officer Shishkin. With the Traveler and Tugarin he slipped into the station, found an untouched Fatui freight list, and tracked the scent of Kristall to a tunnel at Shishkin's house. He then confronted Shishkin publicly with Polonsky's men. Shishkin claimed it was a one-time theft to save his freezing home village of Alatyr. Alyosha exposed the long-running scheme with the mayor and pointed out that Alatyr has been empty for years.

He proved it with "basic math". For months he had counted the carriages on every delivery train and compared their capacity with the town's quota, and one to three carriages were always missing. Polonsky arrested both men and asked whether Alyosha was really a hunter. Because the Fatui had been embarrassed, Alyosha had leverage to get them to put the Traveler's train back on the rails.

5.content: Repnina is an elderly woman from Alatyr who lives in Sretomorozsk. Alyosha met her at a market, they found they came from the same village, and they wrote to each other; her letters first told him about the town's energy problems. Now she has dementia and keeps mistaking him for her grandson. He cleans her stove, brings her Kristall and warmer bedding, and once told her that her long-spoiled berries were delicious rather than disappoint her. He says that as long as she calls him grandson, he is not yet a blurry face in her world.

6.content: Soon after the Traveler's train left Sretomorozsk, it sank into the Shadow Realm. Alyosha recognised it as a place without wind, light or flowing elements, where people vanish or come back changed. He had seen it a few times but never been inside. He could not use his Vision there, so he relied on a few working gadgets and a story about how to escape. With the Eye of Graeae's guidance and a gun it made for the Traveler, they fought through undead Fatui and escaped at Rankova Zorya. He says the Traveler saved his life there.

7.content:
Alyosha guided the Traveler into Snezhnograd by train, showed them the city, and took them to Podvorye Restaurant while he fetched his friend Doctor Luneva for Paimon. He spends most of his time in Zolnyy because the rest of the city is "stunningly expensive"; messages reach him through the boss of the Hunter Trade Station there. He also cleans and moves props at the Korolevskiy Theater, where Odette dances and Vodyanitsa sings.

Thanks to Odette's connections he once worked there as a night watchman and slept in the most expensive VIP box with Tugarin. He found the luxury unsettling next to freezing villages. Asked about his ideal state, he said everyone enjoying a VIP box is a joke, but making sure no one freezes is doable.

8.comment: Alyosha: The theater curse and Ronova
8.content:
In Chapter VII Act II a storm trapped the audience in the Korolevskiy Theater after a performance. After the staff member Dymov failed to return, Alyosha went out alone to check the weather and came back to warn everyone to stay inside. In truth he never came back: Ronova, the Ruler of Death, took his place at that moment and played "Alyosha" for days while people died two by two. The Traveler unmasked her using the folk tale Alyosha himself had told them in Sretomorozsk: death comes in a familiar face. The real Alyosha woke with the others when the afterlife illusion broke.

In the afterlife theater, "Alyosha" found the haunted-theater report, planted the note "Death is near", and used Alyosha's voice to urge Ptashka to stay behind. None of that was the real Alyosha. The Curse of Death triggers when a technological breakthrough could threaten Celestia; this one stemmed from Mitya pondering an innovation during the performance. Victims revive and forget unless something jogs their memory.

9.content:
Following rumours of a gang hoarding Kristall at an abandoned cabin, Alyosha and the Traveler fought through feuding fae gangs. The cabin held Shadow Realm relics instead of Kristall. A fae gang leader came back threatening to blow the place up, and Alyosha disarmed him with Tugarin. Alyosha recognised a machine from a blueprint of the Belyi Tsar's era that he had stolen from fae gangs. Once restarted, it proved to be a prototype Kresnik's Torch, and he turned the cabin into a shelter for Sretomorozsk villagers at risk of freezing. He let the caretaker Chaplina claim she had founded it, because a Rokot member keeps a low profile.

He gave the Traveler the access card and weapon parts they found. A hunter turns back after catching his prey, he said, but an adventurer goes a step further.

10.content:
Alyosha works around Odette at the theater and calls her "Miss Odette". He was surprised that a Fatuus shared the Rokot's principles and took it as a sign that change is easier than he thought. After her break-in at the Armory Palace, he received the Rokot's letter suspending her as Lelek, and he kept working with her anyway. Vodyanitsa is the Rokot's intelligence source at the theater; he relies on her for information but cannot follow her small talk, and wonders whether girls have a secret code.

Odette says he could easily live off hunting alone but takes theater jobs to help others, so she was not surprised he joined the Rokot. Together the three restored life to Rankova Zorya. In 7.1 they hunted the Seal of Life swindler and commissioned a portrait of the Tsaritsa.

11.comment: Alyosha: Seals of Life and Avaz
11.content:
In 7.1 Alyosha joined the crowds giving Seals of Life at the Northland Bank. He does not trust the officials, he said, but will not stand by if the nation is in real danger. When a contact at Central Station began offering "life extension" to the frail and elderly, Vodyanitsa disguised him as an old man. He tracked down the banker Avaz, gained his trust, and caught him with the Traveler, Odette and Vodyanitsa.

Under questioning Avaz threatened to report them to the Veche. Alyosha raised his rifle and wondered aloud whether it counted as extortion when he was not a public official, and Avaz talked. Avaz claimed it went "Harbinger high": seals were missing from the vault, and only Regrator had unrestricted access. Alyosha doubted it at first, since a scheme that went all the way up would not leave one man working alone. They kept Avaz in custody while the Traveler took the matter to the Tsaritsa. The seals were later returned, and Alyosha went back to Sretomorozsk to hunt.

12.content: When the Tsaritsa asked the Traveler, now her special envoy, to collect portraits showing how her people see her, Alyosha came up with the idea for the Rokot's entry. A painter from Fontaine painted her seated among spring flowers, because Snezhnaya is snowbound even in spring and he thought such a picture would warm people's homes. He was not surprised that a Rokot member had become the Tsaritsa's envoy, since they already had a Fatuus. He meant to give the unspent funds to the Rokot.

13.content: In Snezhnograd, Alyosha discovered Genius Invokation TCG and was surprised that a card game was all maths, the subject that once earned him beatings. Medyntsev, a cheerful young merchant who claims to be heir to a family enterprise, beat him. He then described The Cat's Tail in Mondstadt, the Knights of Favonius and songs of freedom. Alyosha asked him what he would do once his plans succeeded, and Medyntsev had no answer, but Alyosha had none for his own question either: what comes after Stuzha? He decided that if he ever leaves Snezhnaya, his first stop will be Mondstadt, both for the card tavern and to study a free and warm nation.

14.content: His father spent a year's savings on the gun and meant to give it to Alyosha when he came of age. Alyosha took it early, on the night of the bandit raid. Since then he has rebuilt it so thoroughly that it is his own. Mitya has also modified it unasked. He maintains it obsessively, because a weapon of any origin can be all that stands between you and death. He once watched a poorly kept gun jam in a lookout's hands and calls that an unhappy gun. He admits that what began as necessity has become a passion that eats his Mora.
